# An agent conversation that carries across re-fires, and restarts in a child graph

An agent node that re-fires inside one frame resumes its own prior session, so a
cascade-driven agent loop keeps its reasoning. A delegated sub-graph's agent
starts from a clean conversation in a run-scope of its own.

## The template

The main graph's agent node subscribes to its own success while its reported
turn is below three, so it re-fires inside one frame. A caller node delegates to
a child graph whose exit is a second agent node.

```yaml
name: session-resume-demo
version: "1"
graphs:
  - name: main
    nodes:
      - type: worker
        executor: claude-agent
        subscribes:
          - node: worker
            type: terminal/success
            force_upstream_refresh: false
            when: "payload.attributes_delta.turn < 3"
        attributes:
          schema:
            type: object
            properties:
              model:         {type: string, default: "claude-sonnet-4-5"}
              system_prompt: {type: string, default: "session continuity"}
              user_prompt:   {type: string, default: "..."}
              cli:           {type: object, default: {}}
              turn:          {type: integer, readOnly: true}
              recall:        {type: string, readOnly: true}

      - type: caller
        delegate: child
        subscribes:
          - node: worker
            type: terminal/success
            force_upstream_refresh: false
            when: "payload.attributes_delta.turn == 3"
        attributes:
          schema: {type: object, properties: {}}

  - name: child
    entry: inner-entry
    exit: inner
    nodes:
      - type: inner-entry
        kind: attribute_passthrough
        attributes:
          schema:
            type: object
            properties:
              opened: {type: boolean, default: true}

      - type: inner
        executor: claude-agent
        subscribes:
          - node: inner-entry
            type: terminal/*
            force_upstream_refresh: false
        attributes:
          schema:
            type: object
            properties:
              model:         {type: string, default: "claude-sonnet-4-5"}
              system_prompt: {type: string, default: "session continuity"}
              user_prompt:   {type: string, default: "..."}
              cli:           {type: object, default: {}}
              turn:          {type: integer, readOnly: true}
              recall:        {type: string, readOnly: true}
```

## Drive it

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/messages" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" -d '{}'

curl -sS "$BASE/v1/observability/events?instance_id=$IID&limit=500"
```

## What the product does

The main-graph agent node runs three times inside one frame, reporting turns 1,
2 and 3.

The first dispatch is spawned fresh. Each later dispatch is spawned resuming the
immediately prior dispatch's session id, so the agent still recalls what the
first turn established. All three dispatches carry the same `run_scope_id`.

A cascade-driven agent loop keeps its reasoning across re-fires instead of
restarting from nothing each time the node wakes.

The child graph's agent node runs once, in a `run_scope_id` different from the
parent's. It is spawned without resuming the parent's session, and its
conversation carries its own memory rather than the parent's.

Delegation resets the reasoning context at the sub-graph boundary — what an
author wants when a child graph is a separate job rather than a continuation of
the caller's turn.
